answer: The Hardware security key bound by in-person pickup code with one identity per channel makes the identity prove its channel on demand: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the in-person pickup code is recorded, and one identity per channel keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a rented or borrowed channel cannot quietly serve ten identities. Like a umber on a key ring, one odd key hides easily, so the check runs on every binding rather than a sample. A quill and a atlas may look alike, but only the identity with a verified channel is honoured.
